com.wac.autocore.test

Class WorkOrderRowsProof

  • java.lang.Object
    • com.wac.autocore.test.WorkOrderRowsProof

  • public final class WorkOrderRowsProof
extends java.lang.Object
    B5: the same work order, created, changed and cancelled, has to leave the same rows in the database no matter who asks for it. Section 2 wants the business to be usable without the window, and that is only worth something if the window and the service layer end up in the same place. A proof cannot open a window, so the window's side is the calls the dialogs make, in their order: the draft and the change as EditDraftDialog makes them, the cancellation as WorkOrderDetailsDialog does it. That side is compared against the same work done through WorkOrderGateway, the narrow entrance from B3. What it catches is the two entrances drifting apart, not a change made inside a dialog. Runs against a copy of the database; the real one is never touched.
